decisions.reason: The client explicitly requires every completed mint's ticket and $5 commission to appear in the recipient NFT's attributes; the resulting one-ticket-per-mint rule also makes the legacy Small/Big ticket-counter attribute obsolete.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
At this point, we have completed 12 mints, so that should amount to 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**Even if no referral code is used, a ticket and commission are still issued**.

Currently, **when a code is used**, it is accurately reflected on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

If **no referral code is used**, the ticket and commission are assigned at random.
(B**ut they must still be reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I believe that since your most recent fix, the randomly assigned tickets from the last 2 mints have been reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
However, the missing tickets have not been backfilled.

The commissions from these purchases without a code are also still not reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot, you will see that I have an NFT showing 2 tickets but only 1 x $5 commission. That should not be possible because each ticket includes a $5 commission.

Also, in my leaderboard screenshot, only 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions are accounted for out of 12 total mints.
Whether or not a referral code is used, 12 mints should result in 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions.

value_updates.ticket_and_commission_attribute_accounti: Each completed mint must be reflected in the recipient NFT's attributes as one ticket and one $5 commission, credited to the code-selected NFT when a referral code is used or to the randomly selected NFT when no referral code is used.

decisions.reason: The reported count of 12 completed mints is context for reward accounting and does not change the existing requirement that public mint statistics match completed mints.
The source specifically requires representation on the leaderboard and NFT attributes, not the dashboard reward summary, whose existing display requirements remain unchanged.
The candidate already requires accurate reward values, while the source specifically identifies NFT attributes and does not necessarily change the separate NFT detail-view requirement.
Ticket and commission attribution does not change which successfully minted NFTs must appear in the user's dashboard listing.
The source concerns reward issuance regardless of referral-code use and does not alter fiat-user wallet provisioning, authentication, notification, or reward-access behavior.

The one-ticket-per-completed-mint rule conflicts with the page's legacy Small/Big ticket copy, but the source does not explicitly request an About-page revision or provide enough current draw details to replace all affected copy safely.
The candidate already requires a $5 commission for each successful no-code mint to be assigned randomly; the source confirms that rule but does not resolve the separate first-mint edge case.
Reward-accounting accuracy does not change NFT cover, image, metadata-asset rendering, or wallet presentation behavior.

The retained FAQ requirements already cover one ticket and one $5 commission and preserve the approved no-code random-allocation explanation; the source does not explicitly request further FAQ copy changes.
Issuance and display of tickets and commissions at mint time do not alter the state transferred when an NFT is sold.
Reward attribution and accounting do not change whether NFT metadata, image, or asset endpoints resolve successfully.
